description:
Background and motivation: We have increasing variability in inbound model manifests (different model sources provide slightly different metadata shapes). That variability makes downstream profile generation and changelog drafting brittle and requires a lot of manual curation. This PR introduces an intake enrichment stage that normalizes and annotates incoming model metadata with conservative affinity hints, stable canonical keys, and provenance traces, plus a changelog curator that uses template-driven human-friendly blurb generation for release notes.

Goals: 1) Reduce manual curation required for onboarding by creating deterministic canonical metadata from noisy inputs. 2) Provide stable affordance tags used by profiling and routing (e.g., "affinity:low_mem", "affinity:fp16_ready"). 3) Generate concise release note snippets automatically to accelerate model rollouts and standardize customer-facing wording.

What this PR changes (high level): - Adds a new enrichment module (ingest/enrichment) with schema_normalizer and transformer adapters for common inbound manifest shapes. - Adds a templated changelog curator (changelog/curator/templater.py) that maps metadata deltas to human-readable snippets with configurable tone and safety filters. - Provides an onboard_backfill CLI to retroactively run enrichment on existing registry entries and emit delta reports. - Exposes a Helm toggle and CI integration to run a small end-to-end integration test for the enrichment path.

Checklist: - [x] schema normalizer core implemented and covered by unit tests - [x] changelog templater with sample templates and safety heuristics - [x] CLI backfill with dry-run mode - [x] docs for operators and maintainers - [x] helm flag and CI integration - [x] reviewer feedback addressed and logging improved

Migration notes/backfill: The onboard_backfill script supports --since and --dry-run flags. For the initial rollout we recommend running a dry-run and sampling 200 manifests, then running in batched mode. The backfill emits a delta CSV and a small sample of generated changelog snippets for signoff.

Risk and fallbacks: Enrichment is opt-in via the helm flag enrichment.enabled=false by default. If any part of the enrichment path fails for a model, the intake falls back to the previous raw-manifest path and logs a bounded warning (we do not block onboarding). The templater includes a conservative whitelist that blocks overly speculative marketing claims.

Tests and CI: Unit tests added for normalizer edge cases and templater heuristics. CI now includes an integration job that runs a containerized mini-registry ingest flow and asserts enrichment idempotency (integration job is green in CI checks).

Related work: This complements ENG-2410 (profiling-affordance-mapping) and reduces the manual curation burden described in PM-98. See docs/registry/enrichment.md for operator guidance and sample outputs.

release_notes: Adds an opt-in intake enrichment pipeline that normalizes inbound model manifests, tags affordance hints for downstream profiling/routing, and a changelog curator that auto-generates concise release note snippets. Includes a backfill CLI and CI integration. Backwards-compatible and opt-in. Recommendations: run dry-run backfill and sample results before mass enabling.
notes_summary: Introduces deterministic metadata enrichment and templated changelog generation to reduce manual onboarding and accelerate model rollouts. Opt-in via helm flag; includes backfill utility and tests.
